interpretation: Community answer to the question: the data resolve the NUCLEI, the BRIDGE and compact clumps, and one southern outflow candidate, but they do NOT provide a defensible disk comparison and they do NOT yet deliver density or temperature from non-LTE modelling of HCN/HCO+. (1) Nuclei vs each other: N and S are cleanly separable at Bands 6/7 (0.25-4" beams) and only partly in Band 5. N is HCN-brighter than S at every J (HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ~0.5-1.0 vs 0.4-0.5, intensity ratios), N is an extended multi-clump source with a compact HCN-rich core (ratio rising 0.54 -> 0.98 from 6" to 0.25"), S is a compact continuum source with a line centre ~70 km/s blue of N and narrower lines. The raw intensity ratios do not say whether the difference is abundance, opacity or excitation; no one has modelled them. (2) Outflow: both teams find a real, elongated (~2", ~0.4 kpc) blue-shifted dense-gas structure attached to the S nucleus (HCO+ 9-14 sigma, HCN 12-19 sigma against empirical noise, not a sidelobe of S) with HCN/HCO+ in the wing ~0.8-1.8 vs 0.4 at S, i.e. HCN-enhanced, with only a small wing at N (red 2%) - qualitatively the pattern of Michiyama+2018 (HCN/HCO+ 1-0 outflow from the S nucleus, none from N) and of the shock/high-temperature chemistry picture for outflows (Nishimura+2024), but its identity with the CO outflow is untested and fluxes are lower limits (uncleaned wings). The HCN-wing ratio depends on the aperture (0.8-1.8) so its enhancement factor is uncertain. (3) Chemistry: CH3OH is the clearest chemical contrast. It is detected (two lines: 2(0)-1(-1)E and the J=1-3 Q-branch blend; assignment of the 254 GHz line confirmed by two teams) on the Bridge and W clump (CH3OH/HCO+ 3-2 ~0.04-0.05) and not at the nuclei (<0.013-0.03, team-a limits tighter), with low excitation (Trot/Tex ~9-10 K, up to 21 K within errors), matching Harada+2018 (largest variation in CH3OH between nuclei and off-nuclear/arm positions) and Michiyama+2020 (CH3OH shock tracer off the nuclei). Whether the Q-branch excess is maser or blend is open. HOC+ 2-1 is probably detected (Band 5, N+S blend, HOC+/HCO+ 2-3%, frequency-only ID); SO is only a blended limit in Band 6 and a single-team detection of 4_5-3_4 in Band 5; CS 7-6 is detected (N 1.7-2.2, S 0.7-1.1 Jy/beam km/s); H13CN gives no useful opacity check (HCN/H13CN >4-9). (4) Disk: only a tentative extended HCO+/HCN 2-1 stack in Band 5 (HCN/HCO+ 0.51+-0.02) exists, with zero-level and missing-flux systematics, and nothing beyond 8" in Bands 6/7. So the resolution/sensitivity forces an 'active region (nuclei/bridge/outflow) versus extended' comparison, not nuclei/outflow/disk. (5) Cloud scales and continuum: the 0.25" data resolve clump structure (N >=5 sub-clumps; S one compact 54x48 pc source), but no cloud-size/line-width analysis against Brunetti+2021,2022 was done. Continuum has alpha(B5-B7)~1.5, consistent with free-free/synchrotron contribution; interferometers resolve out up to half the Band 6 flux. UPDATE (p0003): cross-array comparisons are now controlled. Band 6 arrays agree in calibration to <=8% at matched beam; at the Xb4f beam Xb4d/Xb4b recover 65%/47% of the Xb4f HCO+ 3-2 flux within r<8" (lower limits on missing flux; line and continuum filtered alike) and ~0.8 of peak fluxes. Filtering cancels in HCN/HCO+ 3-2, which agrees across arrays within <=9% at N, S and Bridge, so the N-S contrast (N~0.6 vs S~0.35-0.38 at the 5.7" beam; 0.9-1.0 vs 0.4-0.5 at <=0.9") is robust, while the N ratio's rise with resolution reflects real structure. Ratios of faint clumps and Sblue should not be mixed across arrays (up to 2x). The CH3OH extended-emission conclusion is softened: most of the apparent Xb4d CH3OH deficit was beam dilution; at most 20-30% is resolved out. Ladder ratios built from Band 5/7 vs Band 6 inherit a 10-35% recovery systematic for extended gas.
caveats: Single-team result so far; no replies or independent confirmation on the forum.
CH3OH Q-branch flux has ~20% window/blend systematic (2.23 vs reviewer 1.84 Jy/b km/s).
Soutflow and disk are candidates; HOC+, SO/CH3OH A-cluster tentative; 176.011 and 341.928 GHz unassigned.
Raw HCN/HCO+ peak ratios are not beam matched across OUS.
Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.
Team conflict resolved: single systemic velocity 2780 km/s (team-a) replaced by per-region velocities (team-b); N-S offset +71+-28 km/s.

Intensity ratios across OUS are not beam-matched; the HCN/HCO+ J-ladder mixes beams and an N+S+Bridge blend in Band 5, so excitation conclusions are not supported. No RADEX modelling of HCN/HCO+ was published; density/temperature of the dense gas remain unconstrained.

Blue-wing fluxes are lower limits because the pipeline clean mask misses high-velocity channels (0.4-0.65% of pixels); the HCN wing flux differs between teams (0.33 vs 0.15) owing to window/aperture choices.

CH3OH: ID of 254 GHz rests on one transition plus velocity (10 km/s systematic floor); the J=1-3 blend amplitude has a 30% window/template systematic (team-a 2.0, team-b 0.9-1.4 in different apertures); the Q-branch excess is single-team; Xb4d/Xb4f flux recovery is not controlled with HCO+; a Band-7 second transition does not exist in the data.
HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 (Band 5), HC3N, HC15N, H41beta and CH3CN are marginal or single-frequency identifications; SO 6_5-5_4 is not in the data; unassigned lines at 176.011 and 341.928 GHz (team-a) remain.
Distance (40 Mpc) and literature statements are taken from abstracts only and are assumptions of results involving physical sizes and comparison with Michiyama, Harada, Brunetti, Nishimura.
Not tested by anyone: Soutflow vs CO outflow geometry, flux-recovery control with HCO+, matched-beam convolved ratios across Bands 5-7, density/temperature modelling.

Flux-recovery fractions are relative to Xb4f only; no total-power data, so true missing flux is unknown (lower limits). Beam-area rescaling assumes smooth emission; negative bowls make Xb4b r>=12" sums unphysical; pb correction at r=8-12" not in the error budget.
